nodes.label: Game client
nodes.summary: Pings candidate regions, queues for a mode (solo or party), receives push events, then connects to a dedicated game server.

nodes.label: Game Frontend
nodes.summary: Receives the matchmaking request, authenticates the player, creates a Ticket, and later retrieves the Assignment for it.

nodes.label: Ticket pool
nodes.summary: Each Ticket (mode, rating, region latencies, party) is indexed by its SearchFields and joins the pool Open Match considers for matches.

nodes.label: Director
nodes.summary: Knows the Match Profiles to serve. Periodically calls FetchMatches, then gets a game server from the allocation system and sets the Assignment on every ticket in the match.

nodes.label: Match Function
nodes.summary: Your matching logic: queries tickets that fit a profile and returns Matches. This is where rating and latency rules live, and where search windows widen as tickets age (a design choice).
nodes.details: Open Match's overview says nothing about rating or MMR. Those rules are yours to write.

nodes.label: Evaluator
nodes.summary: Concurrent match functions may propose overlapping matches. The evaluator deduplicates proposals before results return. A default one is provided.

nodes.label: Rating service (TrueSkill-style)
nodes.summary: After a match, updates each player's skill distribution (mean and uncertainty) from team results. Runs asynchronously, off the queue's critical path.
nodes.details: TrueSkill is a Bayesian generalisation of Elo. It tracks uncertainty, models draws, handles any number of entities and infers individual skills from team results. Confirmed: TrueSkill (abstract) tracks uncertainty, models draws and infers individual skill from team results. Running it asynchronously after the match is our design choice.

nodes.label: GameServerAllocation (Agones)
nodes.summary: Atomically allocates a Ready GameServer from a Fleet and moves it to Allocated. Returns address and ports. Selectors are tried in order.
nodes.details: Packed (default) bin-packs for dynamic clusters. Distributed spreads across static ones.

nodes.label: Fleet of warm game servers
nodes.summary: A set of warm GameServers kept Ready or Allocated. Allocated servers stay until SDK.Shutdown() is called or they are deleted.

nodes.label: Dedicated game server
nodes.summary: A Kubernetes Pod running the game. Uses the SDK for lifecycle: Ready when it can accept connections, Shutdown when done.

nodes.label: Lobby chat cluster (per region)
nodes.summary: XMPP-style chat with one session process per player. 6–12 nodes per regional shard sharing only a few fully replicated in-memory tables, so session lookups are local reads.
nodes.details: Riot (2015): offline messages persisted until next login (MySQL legacy, Riak newer shards). Load tests to at least 30 servers.

nodes.label: Messaging service (Edge + Routing)
nodes.summary: Service-to-client push over WebSockets. Edge nodes hold connections. Routing nodes hold the global player-to-edge table and route published messages. Carries match found, ready check and assignment ready events.
nodes.details: Riot's RMS (2017). Using it for matchmaking events is our application of the published design. Confirmed: Riot's RMS pushes service-to-client messages over WebSockets with Edge and Routing tiers. Using it for match-found and ready-check events is our application of that design.

steps.caption: The client asks to queue for a mode. The frontend authenticates the player.
A Ticket (mode, rating, latency to each region, party) joins the pool.
The Director periodically asks for matches for a profile. Open Match runs your Match Function.
The function queries tickets that fit and forms balanced teams. The rating and latency windows widen as tickets wait.
Several functions may propose overlapping matches, so the evaluator deduplicates them.
Surviving matches return to the Director.
The Director requests a game server from the allocation system.
Agones atomically picks a Ready server from the fleet (Packed by default).
The chosen server moves to Allocated and stays until it calls Shutdown.
The Director writes an Assignment (address, ports) onto every ticket in the match.
The frontend returns the Assignment to each client.
The clients connect to the dedicated server and play.
When a match forms, an event is published to the messaging service.
The Edge tier pushes it down each player's WebSocket: match found, accept or decline.
Players in a party or lobby chat. Each player has a session process on a regional chat node, and the routing table is a local read.
The result is sent to the rating service, which updates each player's skill distribution from the team outcome. This runs asynchronously.
